Beállítom Újabb drón lépett be csütörtök hajnalban Románia légterébe az ukrán határ közelében, majd egy lakatlan területen zuhant le Tulcea megyében. A román védelmi minisztérium szerint senki nem sérült meg, és anyagi kár sem keletkezett. A történtek miatt két spanyol F-18-as vadászgépet és egy román katonai helikoptert is riasztottak, közölte a védelmi minisztérium . A minisztérium közleménye szerint a román hadsereg radarjai hajnali 2:23-kor észleltek több légi célpontot az ukrán határ közelében. A helyzet megfigyelésére felszállt a spanyol légierő két F-18-as vadászgépe, valamint a román légierő egy IAR-330 SOCAT helikoptere. A hatóságok hajnali 3:20-kor telefonos RO-Alert riasztást küldtek a környéken élőknek. Egy perccel később a drón Galactól mintegy 13 kilométerre keletre belépett Románia légterébe. A román katonai helikopter személyzete 3:24-kor jelentette, hogy a drón a Tulcea megyei Grindu településtől mintegy négy kilométerre északkeletre, lakatlan területen lezuhant. A becsapódás után tűz keletkezett, amely magától kialudt. Katonákat küldtek a helyszínre, hogy lezárják és átvizsgálják a becsapódás környékét. A készültség hajnali 3:52-kor ért véget. A védelmi minisztérium egyelőre nem közölte, hogy most milyen típusú drón zuhant le, és azt sem, honnan érkezett. Grindu Románia keleti részén, a Duna alsó szakaszán, az ukrán határ közelében fekszik. A térség az ukrajnai háború kezdete óta többször került hasonló helyzetbe : az Ukrajna dunai kikötői ellen végrehajtott támadások idején drónok és drónmaradványok is kerültek már román területre, a hatóságok pedig többször küldtek RO-Alert riasztást a határ mentén élőknek. Az utóbbi napokban több drónos incidens történt Romániában: hétvégén a spanyol légierő F–18-asai lelőttek egy drónt Galac megye felett, amely a NATO szerint minden bizonnyal orosz gyártmányú volt , múlt héten pedig 96 óra alatt több mint száz eszközt észleltek a radarok. http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/.text: Gary Campbell promoted to President, Americas Brian Hatcher promoted to President, Recon, S.E.T., CMFT, Neuro and Biosurgery Bradley Kessler promoted to President, Americas – Robotics, Technology and Data WARSAW, Ind. , Sept. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc. (NYSE and SIX: ZBH), a global medical technology leader, today announced leadership appointments designed to streamline its Americas and Global Business Group organizations for greater focus and agility. Effective October 1, Gary Campbell will be promoted to President, Americas, and Brian Hatcher will be promoted to President, Recon, S.E.T., CMFT, Neuro and Biosurgery. The company also announced the promotion of Bradley Kessler to President, Americas – Robotics, Technology and Data. Campbell, Hatcher and Kessler will report directly to Ivan Tornos, Chairman, President and CEO of Zimmer Biomet. "We talk often about our People and Culture strategic imperative to have the right talent, in the right roles, at the right times," said Tornos. "These well-deserved promotions do exactly that, while helping to accelerate our U.S. go-to-market transformation and sharpen ownership of our most important commercial priorities. Gary, Brian and Brad are seasoned operators and proven Zimmer Biomet leaders with deep experience in the businesses and markets they will now lead. Their promotions reinforce my strong confidence in both our 2026 outlook and our growth potential in 2027 and beyond." As part of this restructuring, Kevin Thornal, Group President, Global Businesses and the Americas, will leave the company on September 30, 2026, following a transition period. Tornos added, "On behalf of the entire Zimmer Biomet team, I want to thank Kevin for his leadership and contributions to our company. We wish him all the best in his next chapter." 2026 Outlook Zimmer Biomet also announced today that the Company is reiterating its full-year 2026 financial outlook provided on August 5, 2026. About Gary Campbell As President, Americas, Campbell will be responsible for commercial strategy and execution across the United States, Canada and Latin America. He will continue to lead the evolution of the company's U.S. go-to-market model, building a specialized and dedicated organization designed to increase productivity and accelerate growth. Campbell has served as Zimmer Biomet's vice president and general manager, Orthopedics – North America since September 2024. Since joining the company in 2019, Campbell has held multiple commercial leadership roles of increasing responsibility. Previously, Campbell served in several sales and marketing roles at Enovis. He holds a bachelor's degree from Texas State University. About Brian Hatcher As President, Recon, S.E.T., CMFT, Neuro and Biosurgery, Hatcher will lead global portfolio strategy and execution across most of the company's businesses, expanding his current remit to include Global Knees and Hips. He will continue to play an integral role in the company's innovation and diversification strategy, including delivering organic and inorganic opportunities in higher growth markets. Lou Galrao, President of Reconstruction (Knees and Hips), will report to Hatcher. During his 16-year career with Zimmer Biomet, Hatcher has held multiple roles in research, marketing, general management and business leadership. He was named to his first Global President role in 2021 and currently serves as Zimmer Biomet's President of S.E.T. and CMFT. Hatcher began his medical technology career with roles at OrbusNeich and later Medtronic. He holds a bachelor's degree in chemistry and a Ph.D. in biomedical engineering, both from the University of Florida. About Brad Kessler As President, Americas – Robotics, Technology and Data, Kessler will be responsible for driving commercial strategy, growth and adoption of the company's broad portfolio of robotics, digital and technology solutions in the Americas, as well as its global service and capital solutions contracting business. Under Kessler's leadership, the company will accelerate the expansion of its specialized robotics salesforce in advance of the highly anticipated launch of the Monogram next-generation orthopedic robot, which is expected in 2027. Kessler brings to the role more than two decades of commercial experience in orthopedics. Currently vice president and general manager, Robotics, Technology and Data Solutions, Kessler has held multiple commercial leadership roles of increasing responsibility since he joined Zimmer Biomet in 2015. Prior to joining Zimmer Biomet, Kessler spent nearly 10 years in sales at Stryker. He holds a bachelor's degree from Texas A&M University and an Executive MBA from the Cox School of Business at Southern Methodist University. About Zimmer Biomet Zimmer Biomet is a global medical technology leader with a comprehensive portfolio designed to maximize mobility and improve health. We seamlessly transform the patient experience through our innovative products and suite of integrated digital and robotic technologies that leverage data, data analytics and artificial intelligence. With 90+ years of trusted leadership and proven expertise, Zimmer Biomet is positioned to deliver the highest quality solutions to patients and providers. Our legacy continues to come to life today through our progressive culture of evolution and innovation. For more information about our product portfolio, our operations in 25+ countries and sales in 100+ countries or about joining our team, visit www.zimmerbiomet.com or follow on LinkedIn at www.linkedin.com/company/zimmerbiomet or X at www.x.com/zimmerbiomet . https://townhall.com/columnists/jeffcrou.text: The Unholy Alliance Between the Media and the Polls Jeff Crouere Nov 02, 2026 12:01 AM Nov 02, 2026 Opinion The opinions expressed by columnists are their own and do not necessarily represent the views of Townhall.com. Advertisement AP Photo/J. Scott Applewhite As the 2026 midterm elections approached, the liberal media breathlessly reported an avalanche of new poll results. The purpose was not to inform, but to influence the election results. Advertisement The clear goal was to emphasize a “blue wave” and the possibility that Democrats would take control of Congress, while suppressing Republican vote totals. The rationale was that bad poll results would discourage Republican voters from participating in the election. They would speculate that their candidate or the GOP had “no chance” because their poll numbers were so low. Consequently, the liberal media magnified announcements from liberals like Professor Larry Sabato when his “Crystal Ball” shifted more U.S. Senate races towards the Democrats. The liberal media did not try to hide their hatred for President Donald Trump or his Make America Great Again (MAGA) agenda. In the first 100 days of his second term, 92 percent of the major media networks’ news stories about the President were negative. Thus, the liberal media used every tool at their disposal to help Democrats, and questionable poll data was an expedient way to harm the chances of Republicans. Because of this unmitigated bias, more Americans need to demand that this misinformation not be disguised as real news. In the 2016 , 2020 , and 2024 elections, polls underestimated support for President Donald Trump. Was this a problem with their methodology or their bias? Most likely, both factors contributed to the inaccurate poll results. Not surprisingly, a new Politico survey found that only 25 percent of Americans believed “political surveys correctly estimate votes.” Additionally, 41 percent of respondents stated that polls tend to “underestimate” either Democrats or Republicans. Recommended Evolution Devolves: A Senile Science That Its Champions Can’t Defend David Klinghoffer Democrats and Republicans, I’ve Got Your Immigration Compromise Right Here Derek Hunter Advertisement Of course, the evidence shows that Republicans are usually the voters underestimated in the homestretch of a major election. In the 2026 midterm campaign, top Republicans were not bashful about blasting the polls. Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson (LA-4) told Fox News that polls were “grossly underestimating Republican enthusiasm around the country…more and more Republicans are unwilling to participate in these surveys.” President Trump called the polls “fake” and “rigged,” while Vice President J.D. Vance said he encourages Republicans to ignore polls because of the “demotivating effect on our voters.” Even polling industry experts like Christine Matthews, President of Bellwether Research, admit her business faces a real challenge. She said, “I do think that non-response among base Republican voters in some of these red states is a problem.” This “problem” must be addressed, for 45 percent of voters admitted that poor poll results may keep them from voting for their preferred candidate. Here is a better idea: let the people make up their own minds without the corrupt media telling them who can win the election. Several European countries ban the release of polling data in the days before an election. In the Czech Republic , the ban lasts several days, but in Luxembourg and Spain it extends for five days. The longest ban is in Italy , where “the law on equal treatment prohibits sharing opinion poll results two weeks before the elections.” Advertisement The laudable “goal is to give voters a period of reflection without being influenced by external elements.” How refreshing. In the United States, our media are intent on limiting the public to considering only those candidates who are “doing well in the polls.” How do Americans know the polling companies are legitimate? Of course, we don’t know, because several fake polling companies released phony results that eager media sources amplified. For example, on October 20, 2026, Wedgewood Polls released a statement admitting to an “experimental project” that involved releasing “fabricated numbers” in polls that media sources such as The New York Times published. In their release , Wedgewood Polls said the purpose of their experiment was “to test a simple hypothesis: How easy is it for an entirely fabricated polling firm to gain traction, to be taken seriously, and expose how little (scrutiny) exists in media and public commentary? The short answer: Far too easy.” Sadly, Wedgewood Polls was not the only fake company exposed during this election cycle. In California, both Median Strategies and SoCal Strategies were exposed as bogus polling companies. In August, representatives of Median Strategies released a strikingly similar statement to the one Wedgewood Polls officials released. They admitted their phony poll data was a “short-term social experiment examining how purported polling information could enter and spread through the political information ecosystem without independent verification.” Advertisement As Republican podcaster Josh Holmes noted , Wedgewood Polls had publicized its so-called data showing Democrats winning Senate races in several key states. He said it was “not a victimless crime” as the information led to a drop in donations and volunteer support for Republican Party candidates. The phony Wedgewood Polls data also destroyed the U.S. Senate candidacy of State Senator Mallory McMorrow (D-MI). She said the bogus results showed her candidacy in single digits, leading to a significant loss of fundraising and volunteer support. She claimed that it showed “Polling is broken.” Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr warned broadcast outlets not to publicize fake poll information. He posted, “Broadcasters are prohibited by the terms of their federal licenses from engaging in News Distortion or promoting Broadcast Hoaxes…broadcasters (must) comply with their public interest obligations. After all, the country benefits greatly when Americans can trust…the media to report the news fairly and accurately.” Another factor in the polling debacle is the use of “text-to-web” results. In previous years, pollsters could reach voters on a landline, but those days are long gone. Today, to reach more voters, pollsters text them an online link. However, as Courtney Kennedy, Senior Vice President of U.S. Public Affairs at Ipsos, noted , this method oversamples younger voters and misses more moderate and conservative voters who are not as tech-savvy. She called this new method “cheap” and said, “You get what you pay for,” which, in essence, is political junk. Advertisement The liberal media is biased, polling is “broken,” and it is time to stop this unholy alliance from influencing our elections.
